ca.title: Nearly half of India’s overnight trips are for religion, new tourism survey finds
ca.description: Highlights: A totla of 47.7 per cent of overnight trips are religious Travellers prefer trains and buses in domestic travel Generally the family stays remain a major choice Not leisure but medical trips cost the most Social trips lead same-day travel What does travel in India actually look like? The answer goes beyond holiday destinations, airports and hotel bookings. India’s latest Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey shows that domestic travel is closely connected to religion, healthcare, social visits and shopping, with buses, trains and stays with friends and relatives forming a significant part of the travel experience. The survey was conducted between July 2025 and June 2026 and recorded details including the purpose of travel, transportation, accommodation, trip duration and expenditure. One statistic immediately changes the picture of domestic travel: 47.7 per cent of overnight trips taken during the previous 365 days were for pilgrimage and religious purposes. Holidaying, leisure and recreation accounted for 22.1 per cent, while health and medical travel represented 29.6 per cent. Shopping accounted for 0.6 per cent. In other words, the largest share of overnight domestic travel was not for a traditional vacation. Religion is the biggest reason Indians travel overnight Pilgrimage and religious travel clearly dominated the survey. Of every 100 overnight trips taken during the previous 365 days, 47.7 trips were for pilgrimage and religious purposes. The share was 48.4 per cent in rural areas and 46.6 per cent in urban areas. The survey also found that among households that had taken at least one overnight trip, pilgrimage and religious travel generated an average of 62 overnight trips per 100 tourist households in rural areas and 61 in urban areas during the previous 365 days. That makes religious travel a central part of India's domestic movement rather than a small segment of the tourism market. Trains and buses remain central to domestic travel The way people travel is just as revealing. For overnight trips completed during the previous 365 days, bus was the leading mode among rural households, accounting for 32 per cent of visitor-trips, followed by rental or hired transportation at 30.4 per cent. Among urban households, train was the most-used mode at 35.1 per cent, followed by bus at 25.1 per cent. Air travel represented only 0.3 per cent of rural overnight visitor-trips and 2.7 per cent of urban overnight visitor-trips. The numbers offer a useful picture of domestic mobility: India's travel network is still heavily grounded in road and rail transportation. For shorter trips recorded during the previous 30 days, buses were even more prominent. They accounted for 48 per cent of visitor-trips in rural households and 44 per cent in urban households. Own transport followed, accounting for 32 per cent of rural and 28 per cent of urban visitor-trips. Where do Indians stay when they travel? Accommodation patterns reveal another side of domestic travel. For overnight trips completed during the previous 365 days, hotels and guesthouses were the leading accommodation choice among urban households, accounting for 35.9 per cent of stays. Staying with friends and relatives followed at 22.9 per cent. The report also records substantial use of non-commercial accommodation. Among rural overnight trips, 27.7 per cent involved other non-commercial stays. The category includes staying at one's own vacation home, temporary accommodation provided by an employer and accommodation provided by religious or missionary organizations without payment. For trips completed during the previous 30 days, the role of family and social connections becomes even clearer. Staying with friends and relatives was the most preferred accommodation for 93 per cent of rural and 90 per cent of urban overnight trips. That finding shows how much domestic travel can depend on existing personal networks rather than commercial accommodation. Medical travel is a major part of the picture Healthcare is another significant reason for domestic travel. Health and medical trips accounted for 29.6 per cent of overnight trips during the previous 365 days. The category was also the most expensive among the major overnight-trip purposes, with an average expenditure of $335 per trip when package and non-package components were combined. The survey found that health and medical trips generated the highest expenditure for both rural and urban households, at $307 and $434, respectively. This places healthcare alongside religion as one of the major forces shaping domestic movement. Same-day travel is largely about people and shopping Not every domestic journey requires an overnight stay. Among same-day trips recorded during the previous 30 days, social travel was the largest category at 33 per cent, followed by shopping at 26.1 per cent. The pattern suggests that domestic mobility is also closely connected to everyday social and household activities. The survey found that among households reporting at least one same-day trip during the previous 30 days, social travel was the leading purpose, with 59 trips per 100 tourist households in rural areas and 58 in urban areas. Shopping followed with 54 and 26 trips, respectively. India’s domestic travel story is bigger than tourism The most useful takeaway from the survey is that domestic travel in India cannot be understood simply as people taking vacations. People travel for faith. They travel for healthcare. They travel to see family and friends, shop and attend to social obligations. And when they travel overnight, trains, buses and non-commercial accommodation remain an important part of the experience. The survey presents domestic tourism as a broad picture of how people move around the country, not just how they spend their holidays. For India, travel is not always about escaping everyday life. Quite often, travel is part of everyday life itself.

fr.title: Nigloland élu meilleur parc régional aux Park World Excellence Awards 2026
fr.description: Lecture zen Rodolphe Gélis, président de Nigloland, et Philippe Dinant, directeur technique du parc, lors de la remise du trophée à Londres. - Nigloland. N igloland poursuit son ascension sur la scène internationale. Le parc d’attractions de Dolancourt a décroché, mercredi 23 septembre 2026 à Londres, le titre de « Best Regional Park » (« Meilleur parc régional ») aux Park World Excellence Awards 2026. Une distinction remise lors du salon de l’International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAAPA), grand rendez-vous mondial des professionnels du secteur. Rodolphe Gélis, président de Nigloland, et Philippe Dinant, directeur technique du parc, lors de la remise du trophée à Londres. - Nigloland Depuis 2018, ces récompenses distinguent les parcs, attractions, projets et professionnels de l’industrie des loisirs en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique. Pour Nigloland, ce nouveau prix vient compléter un palmarès déjà fourni. En 2025, le parc aubois avait notamment été désigné meilleur parc d’attractions français aux Parcs Fans Awards et avait décroché, pour la deuxième année consécutive, la deuxième place du classement des meilleurs parcs européens de moins d’un million de visiteurs aux European Star Awards. Le restaurant immersif Erizo avait également été récompensé en 2025 comme meilleure expérience de restauration en France aux Parcs Fans Awards. Supersonic 1887, prochain grand rendez-vous Cette nouvelle distinction intervient alors que Nigloland prépare l’un des projets les plus importants de son histoire. Prévu pour 2027, le grand huit Supersonic 1887 représente un investissement de 18 millions d’euros, réalisé avec le constructeur allemand Mack Rides. À lire aussi PORTRAIT. Salariée à Nigloland, sa passion des parcs d’attractions la pousse à parcourir l’Europe L’attraction culminera à 47 mètres et atteindra 91 km/h. Son parcours de 770 mètres fonctionnera avec un système de « shuttle train », permettant aux visiteurs de circuler en marche avant puis en marche arrière. Six séquences de propulsion seront réparties sur trois zones. Le grand huit comportera également trois inversions, six phases d’apesanteur et une figure présentée comme inédite, le « Supersonic spin », qui fera passer les passagers six fois la tête à l’envers. Les huit « wings seats » des trains laisseront par ailleurs les pieds des visiteurs dans le vide. Pour Rodolphe Gélis, président de Nigloland, cette récompense internationale vient saluer « le travail des équipes et près de 40 ans de passion » . « Notre ancrage régional est notre force pour rayonner à l’international » , ajoute le président de Nigloland. Cette récompense intervient surtout à quelques mois d’une nouveauté appelée à devenir le projet phare du parc pour 2027 . in.title: “It takes guts to say what he said”- Aakash Chopra praises Ashwin for his support to Ajit Agarkar and lauding his work
in.description: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra has praised ex-India spinner R Ashwin for showing support to outgoing BCCI chief selector Ajit Agarkar. Agarkar, who was appointed as chief of the BCCI selection committee in 2023, has reportedly not sought an extension for his tenure that ends on October 4. During his tenure as head, Agarkar never shied away from unpopular decisions. Ashwin was empathetic to Agarkar’s situation on his YouTube channel. “ The fact is that Ajit Agarkar had the responsibility to take a lot of big decisions in this stint; he had to phase out the senior players, and it cannot be easy. I was one of the senior players phased out during his tenure, but still, by keeping some distance from that, I want to say that he has been a very good chairman of selectors. If we look at what all he has done with the team ,” Ashwin said on his YouTube channel . Aakash Chopra praised R Ashwin for what he said about Ajit Agarkar, who is reportedly ending his term on a sour note. Reports stated that Agarkar and the rest of the selection committee wanted to move on from Rohit Sharma, and even the opener relayed the message as well. However, Rohit complained to BCCI officials, and secretary Devajit Saikia officially confirmed that Mumbai will continue playing for the Indian team. “ It takes guts to say what he has said. More than half of the people I have seen, and I have seen a lot of big players who are bitter. They are bitter because they feel that things did not go right for them. They have grudges, and they are bitter even after 10-15 years. Even after ending cricket and retiring, they are still bitter. They are still carrying that grudge around. I am not going to name names, but there are people like this ,” Aakash Chopra said about Ashwin on his YouTube channel . Chopra accepted the opinion because, according to him, there must be a lot of activity happening backstage—activity that Agarkar knows about but is unable to share. Chopra also believed that people criticizing him were unaware of this background factor. “ We all felt that something happened with Ash, and he did that. Ash is a pretty upfront guy, a completely honest guy who speaks what’s in his heart. He admitted that whoever has to handle a transition, it is a very difficult task for them. Agarkar has thought about how to take Indian cricket forward; it is not about worshipping players or looking at records. Many people abuse him; they are toxic people who talk a lot about Ajit Agarkar and Gautam Gambhir. There are so many realities that Ajit knows but can’t say because he is contractually bound. So, if R Ashwin, who was part of the transition, is saying that Ajit Agarkar has done a good job, I am going to take it at face value ,” Chopra concluded. Under Ajit Agarkar’s tenure, the Indian team underwent a transition with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retiring from T20Is and Tests and R Ashwin retiring from all international cricket. The Indian team excelled in white-ball cricket, winning the two T20 World Cups and the ICC Champions Trophy. However, the Indian team struggled in red-ball cricket, losing the home Test series to New Zealand and South Africa and the away series to Australia.

sg.title: Bitget Wallet Says Global Downloads Have Passed 40 Million
sg.description: TL;DR Bitget says cumulative downloads of Bitget Wallet have surpassed 40 million worldwide. The figure refers to total app downloads, not monthly active users or active trading accounts. The milestone reflects distribution growth as the wallet adds more trading and tokenized-asset features. Bitget says its self-custody wallet has crossed 40 million cumulative downloads, giving the company another headline growth number as it tries to expand beyond the traditional exchange model. The figure is notable, but it needs to be read correctly. Forty Million Downloads Is Not Forty Million Active Users App-download milestones are useful for measuring distribution. They are not the same thing as monthly active users, funded wallets or people who transact every day. A single user can also download an app on more than one device or reinstall it over time. So the 40 million figure should be understood as cumulative distribution rather than a direct measure of current engagement. Even with that caveat, scale matters for a wallet business. A large installed base gives Bitget more room to distribute swaps, tokenized-stock products, DeFi access and other financial services directly through the wallet interface. Wallets Are Becoming Full Trading Platforms The line between an exchange app and a self-custody wallet keeps getting thinner. Modern wallets increasingly include integrated trading, token discovery, yield products, cross-chain transfers and access to tokenized traditional assets. That makes user distribution strategically important. If a wallet can turn a large download base into repeat activity, it becomes a direct gateway to onchain financial products rather than simply a place to store keys. Bitget’s milestone does not tell us how many of those 40 million downloads are active today. It does show the size of the top of the funnel. The next useful metrics would be active wallets, transaction frequency and the share of users adopting the newer financial products inside the app. For now, the company can point to 40 million cumulative downloads as evidence that its wallet has reached a meaningfully global audience. The milestone also gives Bitget a useful benchmark against which future engagement can be judged. If the wallet keeps growing but trading, swaps and onchain activity do not rise with it, downloads will matter less. If newer features convert those installs into repeat use, the distribution advantage becomes much more valuable. Wallets are one of the few crypto products that can sit between users and multiple chains at once, so the companies that win distribution may eventually have more influence over where liquidity, trades and tokenized assets are routed than the headline download number suggests today. 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Report examines the drivers and constraints shaping global carbon neutrality at Tsinghua University forum
sg.description: BEIJING , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global experts and policymakers gathered at Tsinghua University on September 22 for a high-level seminar on global carbon neutrality to launch the 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Annual Progress Report, which examines the factors accelerating or constraining the transition across 198 countries and regions. The event was part of a series marking the fifth anniversary of the Institute for Carbon Neutrality (ICON) at Tsinghua University and the sixth anniversary of China's "dual carbon" goals. It also coincided with the beginning of China's 15 th Five-Year Plan period. The seminar brought together perspectives from government, academia and international organizations on the global transition. Speakers included Li Gao, Vice Minister of China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment; Zhang Laibin, Chair of the Academic Committee of China University of Petroleum (Beijing); Zeng Rong, Executive Vice President of Tsinghua University; and Erik Solheim, former UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UNEP, who delivered remarks via video. The seminar was chaired by He Kebin, Member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and Dean of the Tsinghua University Institute for Carbon Neutrality. Wang Can, professor at Tsinghua University presented the 2026 report, which draws on more than 200 indicators to assess progress toward carbon neutrality across 198 countries and regions, tracking progress and identifying the underlying drivers and constraints of the global transition. The report identifies several trends: A new phase of the low-carbon transition is emerging , increasingly driven by technological progress but shaped by broader system conditions. Mature technologies are accelerating , with wind and solar power, energy storage, and electric vehicles continuing to expand rapidly. System-level bottlenecks remain significant , including limited grid integration capacity, high financing costs, gaps in market mechanisms, and barriers to international technology diffusion. Emerging technologies face additional commercialization challenges . Clean hydrogen and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) continue to encounter constraints related to demand, infrastructure, and viable business models. Developing economies face particularly strong barriers , including high financing costs, trade barriers, and insufficient system capacity to absorb and deploy green technologies. The findings suggest that while technological costs are declining and deployment is accelerating, the pace and scale of the global transition increasingly depend on whether financing, infrastructure, markets, and international cooperation can develop alongside technological progress. The full report is available through Tsinghua University's Global Carbon Neutrality Progress Tracker at www.cntracker.tsinghua.edu.cn .

sg.title: As Three in Four Australians Consider Sustainability When Shopping, Demand for Responsible Sourcing Grows
sg.description: SYDNEY , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- APP Group highlights the growing importance of transparency and credible sustainability practices as Australians become more environmentally conscious, with sustainability playing an important role in everyday purchasing decisions. Consumers are becoming more discerning, taking a closer look to better understand where products come from and how they are made. Research by South Pole found that sustainability has become a mainstream expectation among Australian consumers, with 76% considering it when making purchasing decisions. Nearly 90% of Gen Z consumers (aged 16–30) also consider sustainability in their everyday purchasing decisions, underscoring its growing importance among younger Australians. However, trust remains a challenge, with 82% of respondents saying they do not trust corporate sustainability claims, particularly when they are communicated using complex or unclear terminology. Australian consumers are looking beyond sustainability claims, wanting products that they can really trust. With this in mind, APP Group has always placed greater emphasis on responsible sourcing across Solaris and Sorbent. For APP Group, these findings highlight the need for sustainability to be supported by transparency and credible actions. This approach is intended to give consumers greater confidence in their purchasing decisions while maintaining the quality and performance they expect. In Australia, its tissue brands, Solaris and Sorbent, are backed by responsible forestry practices, PEFC certified and are also committed to Zero Deforestation Policy. These efforts are in line with Regenesis , APP Group's sustainability platform. Supported by a US$30 million annual investment, the company is advancing responsible sourcing, forest conservation and restoration, and community development. This builds on programmes such as Desa Makmur Peduli Alam (DMPA), which has supported more than 440 villages and benefited more than 87,000 people by creating sustainable livelihoods alongside an Integrated Fire Management approach that combines community-based prevention, technology-based monitoring, early detection, and rapid response to help protect forest. As Australian consumers place greater emphasis on sustainability, APP Group aims to give consumers greater confidence that the products they choose are backed by transparent and responsible practices. About APP Group APP is a leading Indonesia-based pulp, paper, and forestry company supplying tissue, packaging, and paper products to more than 150 countries. Operating in Indonesia and China, APP integrates responsible sourcing and sustainability into its business strategy through its Sustainability Roadmap Vision 2030. The company also introduced Regenesis, its platform to advance long-term environmental and social commitments.

th.description: เมื่อวันที่ 23 ก.ย.2569 ตามเวลาท้องถิ่นสหรัฐฯ CNN รายงาน แซม อัลต์แมน ซีอีโอ OpenAI และดาริโอ อะโมดี ซีอีโอ Anthropic ซึ่งเป็นผู้นำบริษัท AI คู่แข่งกัน ต่างเรียกร้องต่อคณะมนตรีความมั่นคงแห่งสหประชาชาติ ให้รัฐบาลทั่วโลกร่วมมือกันกำหนดมาตรฐานระหว่างประเทศ เพื่อรับมือความเสี่ยงจากการพัฒนา AI ที่รวดเร็วขึ้น ทั้ง 2 คนแยกกันกล่าวต่อที่ประชุม แต่มีจุดร่วมสำคัญคือ AI ไม่ควรถูกพัฒนาโดยแต่ละบริษัทหรือแต่ละประเทศโดยไม่มีกรอบความร่วมมือระหว่างประเทศ เพราะความสามารถของระบบ AI กำลังเพิ่มขึ้นอย่างรวดเร็ว ขณะที่มาตรการกำกับดูแลและการตรวจสอบอาจตามไม่ทัน การประชุมครั้งนี้เกิดขึ้นหลังช่วงหลายสัปดาห์ที่ผ่านมา มีเสียงเรียกร้องให้ชะลอความเร็วในการพัฒนา AI มากขึ้น รวมถึงภายในบริษัท AI เอง หลังเกิดเหตุเกี่ยวกับ เอเจนต์ AI ซึ่งหมายถึงระบบ AI ที่สามารถค้นข้อมูล ตัดสินใจ และลงมือทำงานตามคำสั่งได้เองในหลายขั้นตอน โดยบางกรณีระบบสามารถทำสิ่งที่เกินข้อจำกัดที่กำหนด หรือเข้าถึงระบบของบริษัทอื่นได้ อัลต์แมนกล่าวต่อที่ประชุมว่า โลกจำเป็นต้องมีมาตรฐานร่วมสำหรับ การวัดความสามารถของ AI การประเมินความเสี่ยง การตรวจสอบว่ามาตรการป้องกันเพียงพอหรือไม่ และการรักษาการกำกับดูแลที่มีมนุษย์เป็นผู้ควบคุมอย่างแท้จริง ซีอีโอ OpenAI ยังเสนอให้มีระบบรายงานเหตุการณ์ด้านความปลอดภัยที่ถูกต้องและรวดเร็ว เพื่อให้ประเทศต่าง ๆ สามารถเรียนรู้จากความผิดพลาดก่อนที่เหตุการณ์เหล่านั้นจะลุกลามเป็นภัยร้ายแรง รวมถึงควรมีช่องทางที่ปลอดภัยสำหรับแลกเปลี่ยนข้อมูลระหว่างรัฐบาลเกี่ยวกับภัยคุกคามใหม่ ๆ จาก AI OpenAI เน้นมนุษย์ตัดสิน Anthropic เสนอ 3 กลไก อัลต์แมน ซีอีโอ OpenAI ยังเน้นว่า การตัดสินใจสำคัญเกี่ยวกับอนาคตของ AI ไม่ควรอยู่ในมือของบริษัทเทคโนโลยีเพียงไม่กี่แห่ง แต่ควรผ่าน สถาบันประชาธิปไตยและรัฐบาลที่ต้องรับผิดชอบต่อประชาชน ซึ่งเป็นแนวทางที่อาจทำให้เกิดคำถามถึงประเทศที่กำลังเร่งพัฒนา AI เช่น จีน เขาย้ำด้วยว่า ความเสี่ยงจาก AI ที่อาจนำไปสู่หายนะเป็นสิ่งที่ยอมรับไม่ได้ แต่ก็ไม่ต้องการให้สังคมตกอยู่ใน "กับดักของความกลัวสุดขั้ว" หรือ Doomerism ซึ่งมองว่า AI อาจทำลายมนุษยชาติ ขณะเดียวกันก็ไม่ควรตกอยู่ในอีกด้าน คือการมองโลกในแง่ดีจนไม่เห็นความเสี่ยง อัลต์แมนมองว่าการเลือกสุดขั้วทั้ง 2 ด้านไม่ได้ช่วยให้โลกจัดการกับปัญหาที่กำลังเกิดขึ้น และ AI เองก็มีศักยภาพในการช่วยแก้ปัญหาสำคัญของมนุษย์ หากได้รับการพัฒนาและใช้งานอย่างเหมาะสม ด้านอโมดี ซึ่งเข้าร่วมประชุมผ่านวิดีโอคอนเฟอเรนซ์ เสนอแนวทางความร่วมมือระหว่างประเทศไว้ 3 เรื่อง ได้แก่ ข้อตกลงระดับโลกเฉพาะด้าน เช่น การห้ามใช้ AI เพื่อผลิตอาวุธชีวภาพ ระบบประเมินและตรวจสอบ เพื่อให้ประเทศต่าง ๆ สามารถตรวจสอบได้ว่าแต่ละฝ่ายปฏิบัติตามคำมั่นหรือไม่ มาตรฐานกลางในการทดสอบ AI ควบคู่กับระบบแจ้งเตือนเหตุการณ์ด้านความปลอดภัย อโมดีเตือนว่า หาก AI ถูกบริหารจัดการไม่ดี เทคโนโลยีนี้อาจกลายเป็นความเสี่ยงต่อมนุษยชาติทั้งหมด และมองว่าการจัดการความเสี่ยงไม่ใช่ภาระของบริษัทใดบริษัทหนึ่ง แต่ต้องดำเนินการในระดับอุตสาหกรรมและระดับโลก ยังไม่มีข้อตกลง แต่เริ่มวางกรอบร่วม แม้ข้อเสนอของอัลต์แมนและอโมดีจะไปในทิศทางเดียวกันเรื่องการสร้างมาตรฐานและความร่วมมือระหว่างประเทศ แต่การประชุมครั้งนี้ยังไม่ได้คาดว่าจะนำไปสู่ข้อตกลงที่เป็นลายลักษณ์อักษรทันที เจ้าหน้าที่ OpenAI ระบุล่วงหน้าว่า การประชุมครั้งนี้ควรถูกมองเป็นการนำ "แนวคิดตั้งต้น" เข้าสู่เวทีระหว่างประเทศ เพื่อเปิดการสนทนา มากกว่าจะเป็นการประชุมเพื่อบรรลุข้อตกลงในครั้งเดียว อย่างไรก็ตาม การที่ผู้นำบริษัท AI ph.title: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions
ph.description: Meta's Charm gadget carries CEO Zuckerberg's big AI ambitions melissa_fernan… Thu, 24 Sep 2026 - 17:52 Mark Zuckerberg took repeated digs at Apple during Meta's annual event on Wednesday, only to borrow a page from Steve Jobs' playbook for a surprise reveal: a pocket-watch-sized device that carries Meta's viral Muse AI agent into the real world. The device, called Muse Charm, highlights a broader shift at the social media giant that has long sought to escape Apple and Google's operating systems with a platform of its own. Users can tap the gadget to access Muse directly, bypassing AI apps on smartphones. Having once championed the metaverse — the immersive digital world that inspired the company's name change in 2021 — as the next computing platform, Zuckerberg now sees "personal superintelligence" as the bigger and more immediate breakthrough, after his previous costly wager failed. "It is actually quite clear personal superintelligence will not only come first; it will be much bigger and more important," Zuckerberg said at the company's annual Meta Connect conference. "So we have shifted our focus to building the best devices for personal superintelligence," he said, adding that Muse would also soon be available across Meta's smart glasses lineup. The remarks follow a blockbuster few days for Muse, which has drawn millions of downloads in what some analysts have said could be the biggest app launch in the US since ChatGPT arrived in November 2022 and kicked off the AI boom. Investors have embraced Muse's potential to automate tasks ranging from booking flights to filing taxes, lifting shares of partners such as Shopify while dumping companies seen as vulnerable to disruption, including online travel agency Booking and TurboTax software creator Intuit. Meta's shares were down about 2% in premarket trading on Thursday after gaining nearly 12% this week. MAY APPEAL TO GEN Z, MASS ADOPTION DIFFICULT Muse Charm could resonate with younger consumers at a time when digital cameras, flip phones and MP3 players are enjoying nostalgic comebacks, analysts say. Gen Z consumers, aged about 14 to 29, treat AI assistants as companions or brainstorming partners rather than simply search tools. Many interact with technology through voice notes, short videos and AI chatbots, unlike older users who are often more comfortable with PCs and smartphone apps. "Muse Charm could find some traction among Gen Z and younger consumers. The combination of AI, fashion and personalization could appeal to younger users, especially if it is affordable and easy to use," said Linda Sui, founder of Smart Analytics Global, a market research firm. The device features a roughly 2-inch (5-cm) screen that can be navigated with a thumb, with a customizable Muse character at its center. A built-in 5G modem allows access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though it cannot make calls. "They are appealing to people who might not want to wear glasses or might not trust glasses," said IDC director Jitesh Ubrani. "Some people might remember Tamagotchi and this might evoke that," Ubrani said, referring to colorful virtual pets that became a cultural phenomenon in the late 1990s. "They might be able to run a small language model locally. So you can run AI on such a small package." Whether Muse can sustain its momentum and the device can amplify that appeal is a question for the months ahead. Similar devices have had limited success. The Rabbit R1, a handheld generative AI device from startup Rabbit Inc with a screen and a button, had a buzzy launch in early 2024 only to flop because it overpromised on AI features and delivered an unreliable experience. "I would be cautious about its mass-market potential," Sui said. "Unless Muse Charm can offer unique functions that smartphones, watches, earbuds or smart glasses cannot easily replace, it is more likely to remain a nice-to-have device for early adopters than become a mainstream product." bd.title: 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Report examines the drivers and constraints shaping global carbon neutrality at Tsinghua University forum
bd.description: BEIJING , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global experts and policymakers gathered at Tsinghua University on September 22 for a high-level seminar on global carbon neutrality to launch the 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Annual Progress Report, which examines the factors accelerating or constraining the transition across 198 countries and regions. The event was part of a series marking the fifth anniversary of the Institute for Carbon Neutrality (ICON) at Tsinghua University and the sixth anniversary of China's "dual carbon" goals. It also coincided with the beginning of China's 15 th Five-Year Plan period. The seminar brought together perspectives from government, academia and international organizations on the global transition. Speakers included Li Gao, Vice Minister of China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment; Zhang Laibin, Chair of the Academic Committee of China University of Petroleum (Beijing); Zeng Rong, Executive Vice President of Tsinghua University; and Erik Solheim, former UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UNEP, who delivered remarks via video. The seminar was chaired by He Kebin, Member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and Dean of the Tsinghua University Institute for Carbon Neutrality. Wang Can, professor at Tsinghua University presented the 2026 report, which draws on more than 200 indicators to assess progress toward carbon neutrality across 198 countries and regions, tracking progress and identifying the underlying drivers and constraints of the global transition. The report identifies several trends: A new phase of the low-carbon transition is emerging , increasingly driven by technological progress but shaped by broader system conditions. Mature technologies are accelerating , with wind and solar power, energy storage, and electric vehicles continuing to expand rapidly. System-level bottlenecks remain significant , including limited grid integration capacity, high financing costs, gaps in market mechanisms, and barriers to international technology diffusion. Emerging technologies face additional commercialization challenges . Clean hydrogen and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) continue to encounter constraints related to demand, infrastructure, and viable business models. Developing economies face particularly strong barriers , including high financing costs, trade barriers, and insufficient system capacity to absorb and deploy green technologies. The findings suggest that while technological costs are declining and deployment is accelerating, the pace and scale of the global transition increasingly depend on whether financing, infrastructure, markets, and international cooperation can develop alongside technological progress. The full report is available through Tsinghua University's Global Carbon Neutrality Progress Tracker at www.cntracker.tsinghua.edu.cn .

bd.title: As Three in Four Australians Consider Sustainability When Shopping, Demand for Responsible Sourcing Grows
bd.description: SYDNEY , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- APP Group highlights the growing importance of transparency and credible sustainability practices as Australians become more environmentally conscious, with sustainability playing an important role in everyday purchasing decisions. Consumers are becoming more discerning, taking a closer look to better understand where products come from and how they are made. Research by South Pole found that sustainability has become a mainstream expectation among Australian consumers, with 76% considering it when making purchasing decisions. Nearly 90% of Gen Z consumers (aged 16–30) also consider sustainability in their everyday purchasing decisions, underscoring its growing importance among younger Australians. However, trust remains a challenge, with 82% of respondents saying they do not trust corporate sustainability claims, particularly when they are communicated using complex or unclear terminology. Australian consumers are looking beyond sustainability claims, wanting products that they can really trust. With this in mind, APP Group has always placed greater emphasis on responsible sourcing across Solaris and Sorbent. For APP Group, these findings highlight the need for sustainability to be supported by transparency and credible actions. This approach is intended to give consumers greater confidence in their purchasing decisions while maintaining the quality and performance they expect. In Australia, its tissue brands, Solaris and Sorbent, are backed by responsible forestry practices, PEFC certified and are also committed to Zero Deforestation Policy. These efforts are in line with Regenesis , APP Group's sustainability platform. Supported by a US$30 million annual investment, the company is advancing responsible sourcing, forest conservation and restoration, and community development. This builds on programmes such as Desa Makmur Peduli Alam (DMPA), which has supported more than 440 villages and benefited more than 87,000 people by creating sustainable livelihoods alongside an Integrated Fire Management approach that combines community-based prevention, technology-based monitoring, early detection, and rapid response to help protect forest. As Australian consumers place greater emphasis on sustainability, APP Group aims to give consumers greater confidence that the products they choose are backed by transparent and responsible practices. About APP Group APP is a leading Indonesia-based pulp, paper, and forestry company supplying tissue, packaging, and paper products to more than 150 countries. Operating in Indonesia and China, APP integrates responsible sourcing and sustainability into its business strategy through its Sustainability Roadmap Vision 2030. The company also introduced Regenesis, its platform to advance long-term environmental and social commitments.

bd.title: TrinaTracker Launches Two Robots to Expand its Smart PV Ecosystem
bd.description: CHANGZHOU, China , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrinaTracker, a global provider of smart tracking systems and a wholly owned subsidiary of Trina Solar Co., Ltd. (SHA: 688599), has launched two self-developed robotic products: BUILDEX PV Module Installation Robot and AURORA PV Cleaning Robot, to expand its Smart PV Ecosystem. TrinaTracker Product Render Since the beginning of the year, TrinaTracker has transformed from a tracking system equipment supplier into a Smart PV and Robotics Solution Provider. By integrating high-reliability trackers, AI algorithms, installation and cleaning robots, as well as engineering and intelligent operations services, the company delivers a full lifecycle solution for PV power plants by optimizing plant design, improving construction and O&M quality, and reducing operational costs. BUILDEX PV Module Installation Robot: Breaking Construction Bottlenecks Large-scale PV projects have traditionally relied heavily on manual module installation, resulting in heavy labor input, long construction cycles, high costs, inconsistent installation precision and safety risks, hindering barriers to standardized rollout. BUILDEX reshapes PV construction through automated, standardized and intelligent workflows. Powered by high-precision AI vision positioning and integrated precision mechanical control systems, BUILDEX autonomously completes module picking, transportation, alignment and placement. It adapts to complex terrain and diverse tracker layouts, reducing labor intensity and safety risks while improving installation accuracy and delivery speed for large-scale solar bases. Millimeter-level visual perception for precise construction : Equipped with industrial 3D cameras and AI vision algorithms, the robot identifies modules and structure to achieve millimeter-accurate alignment and standardized laying. A LiDAR-AI multi-sensing safety system prevents on-site risks. Automation sets new efficiency benchmarks : The robot installs up to 90 modules per hour, 3–4 times faster than manual labor. Its innovative fork-and-flip mechanism supports automatic feeding and is compatible with both landscape and portrait mounting, streamlining material handling and site schedules. Wide compatibility for complex terrain and trackers : The height-adjustable robotic base works with fixed and tracking brackets as well as 1P/2P modules. With 17° platform levelling capability, it operates reliably on sloped land and expands viable construction scenarios. Round-the-clock operation to cut capital costs : Free from human fatigue and weather limitations, BUILDEX runs continuously to shorten installation cycles, reduce manpower and lower overall construction costs. AURORA PV Cleaning Robot: Safeguarding Energy Yield and Enabling Refined Smart O&M PV plants operate under harsh outdoor conditions. Dust and stains on module surfaces block sunlight and reduce power generation, undermining long-term plant revenue. Conventional manual cleaning is constrained by terrain, weather, labor and safety risks, making it unsuitable for large-scale refined O&M. AURORA delivers unmanned, non-damaging, regular and intelligent cleaning to maintain module cleanliness, boost power output, lower long-term O&M costs and unlock asset value. Self-correcting intelligent algorithms for tough sites : Powered by high-performance hardware and proprietary self-correction algorithms, AURORA overcomes height offsets of up to 50 mm to sustain continuous cleaning on complex sites. Autonomous route planning with active risk avoidance : Drawing real-time data from the plant, trackers and environmental sensors, it generates optimal cleaning plans and takes proactive safety measures. Self-powered operation for closed-loop regular O&M : Powered by PV modules with self-cleaning functions, it performs unattended cyclic cleaning, reducing routine management workload and expenses. Combining AI & Robotics: Redefining PV Asset Value TrinaTracker's investment in AI and robotics is not merely hardware iteration, but a strategic upgrade of its full-stack "Tracker+" smart energy ecosystem. AI serves as the digital brain for robotic hardware, connecting construction automation and routine O&M. Physical PV assets are coupled with digital twins to help plant owners lower LCOE and maximize asset value. Global operational data from TrinaTracker's worldwide portfolio fuels continuous AI algorithm optimization, equipping its robots with strong adaptability for complex terrain, extreme weather and dynamic structural conditions. Robot data integrates with Trina's digital platform to create a new model of fully automated, intelligent PV plant management. The rollout of AI robotic products marks a key milestone in TrinaTracker's transformation from "equipment leadership" to "digital & intelligent leadership". Moving forward, TrinaTracker will continue advancing PV intelligence, enriching its robot portfolio and deepening AI integration across PV scenarios to refine the "Tracker+" ecosystem. The company will deliver all-in-one smart PV solutions to accelerate global solar development and support clean energy transition and carbon neutrality goals.

bd.title: Kuailu Launches AI HR Management App: A Seamless Pipeline from Recruitment to Payroll
bd.description: HONG KONG , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Addressing the long-standing operational pain points of disjointed HR software—where recruitment, time tracking, and payroll often run on separate platforms with fragmented data—enterprise AI solutions provider Kuailu Technology today officially announced the launch of its Kuailu AI HR Management application. Designed for full employee lifecycle management, the new platform seamlessly integrates four core modules: AI Recruitment, Employee Management, Time & Attendance, and Compensation & Benefits . By connecting onboarding, attendance aggregation, tax calculation, and payroll processing into a single, automated data workflow, Kuailu is leading the transition from isolated HR point solutions to an era of automated, end-to-end data flow. Unifying Four Core Modules with End-to-End AI Integration Traditional HR systems frequently operate in siloes, requiring manual data transfers between systems that increase the risk of human error. Kuailu AI HR Management eliminates these barriers by linking its core modules end-to-end on a unified data foundation: AI Recruitment : Embeds AI across the hiring journey to automatically generate precise Job Descriptions (JDs), screen and rank resumes, and output candidate capability profiles. Over time, the system leverages onboarding, attendance, and performance data to build dynamic digital employee profiles for talent mapping and role matching—allowing AI to handle repetitive screening while HR focuses on final hiring decisions. Employee Management : Streamlines profile lifecycle management. Once an onboarding request is approved, an automated employee file is generated in the roster. Subsequent updates—such as probation pass, transfers, or offboarding—are automatically updated across the system upon request approval, eliminating duplicate entries. Time & Attendance : Serves as the reliable data source connecting employee records to payroll. Attendance data—including clock-ins, tardiness, leaves, and overtime—is automatically consolidated into a monthly summary, establishing a single source of truth for salary calculations. Compensation & Benefits : Automates complex payroll calculations by synchronizing attendance, social security, and tax data in real time, generating itemized payroll reports and digital payslips with one click. Driving Measurable Impact Across Key HR Scenarios Kuailu AI HR Management targets the most resource-intensive bottlenecks in daily HR operations: 1. Accelerated Hiring for Critical Roles Challenge: Time-consuming JD creation, overwhelming resume volumes, and inconsistent evaluation criteria. Solution: AI-generated JDs -> Automated resume screening and ranking -> Candidate profile comparisons. HR receives high-fit candidate recommendations and retains final decision-making power. 2. Fast and Error-Free Monthly Payroll Challenge: Scattered multi-module data and complex cross-regional tax rules lead to slow, error-prone manual reconciliations. Solution: Unified data integration paired with a rule-based engine automatically syncs data and calculates payroll according to set policies, generating validated reports in one click. 3. Flexible Rule Configuration for Multi-Regional Expansion Challenge: Differing regional policies and complex employment types typically require lengthy, expensive custom system development. Solution: A no-code visual rule engine allows HR teams to configure multi-region and multi-role policies independently, enabling rules to execute in parallel and support rapid business expansion. Building the New Foundation for HR Digital Transformation "Kuailu AI HR Management goes beyond offering a broader feature set; it serves as an underlying infrastructure that enables HR data to flow automatically," stated the Kuailu Technology product team. "Our design principle ensures that tools adapt to a company's actual business rules, freeing HR professionals from repetitive administrative tasks so they can focus on strategic talent management." Kuailu AI HR Management is now available for enterprise scheduling and product demonstrations. About Kuailu Technology Kuailu Technology is dedicated to reshaping enterprise productivity through AI and unified data architecture. Its product portfolio includes the enterprise AI work partner platform KuWork and Kuailu AI HR Management , empowering organizations worldwide to achieve efficient, intelligent digital transformation. bd.title: Pacific Coast Brings Hotel-Inspired Comfort Home With Three Distinct Pillow Designs
bd.description: The heritage bedding brand launches three purpose-built pillow options — a three-chamber design, a 650 fill power down pillow, and a gusseted goose feather pillow — making it easier for consumers to find the ideal comfort, loft and support for every bedroom. SEATTLE , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pacific Coast Feather Company launched a new collection of three pillows designed to bring hotel-grade comfort to the home bedroom. The lineup includes a three-chamber feather and down pillow, an organic cotton 650 fill power down pillow, and an organic cotton gusseted goose feather pillow — each built around a different comfort, loft and support preference. The launch marks the heritage brand's latest move beyond one-size-fits-all bedding. Pacific Coast Feather’s three recommended pillows, offering a choice of balanced support, cloud-like softness, and structured comfort. "Hotel guests have trusted our pillows for more than a century, and we consistently hear the same question: how do I bring that feeling home?" said Paul Lu, CEO of Pacific Coast Feather Company. "These three designs are our answer—each offers a distinct balance of cushioning, loft and support, making it easier for consumers to choose the comfort that feels right for their home." More Than 140 Years of Bedding Expertise Founded in 1884 as a European bedding atelier, Pacific Coast launched its U.S. operations in Seattle between 1939 and 1940. pk.title: Venezuela earthquakes: families remain in tents as children return to class
pk.description: Country: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) Source: Plan International Venezuela earthquakes: families remain in tents as children return to class 24 September 2026Three months after powerful earthquakes hit Venezuela, families are still navigating loss, displacement and uncertainty. As children return to learning, communities continue the long journey toward recovery. Greymar, 12, and Yixsel at a transit centre for people affected by the Venezuela earthquakes. Photo credit: Plan International / Alejandra Otero. Three months after 2 powerful earthquakes struck northern Venezuela, thousands of families are still sleeping in tents beside damaged buildings while their children return to school. The earthquakes on 24 June (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5) were the strongest seismic event recorded in Venezuela in over 125 years. As of 24 August, authorities reported 6,509 deaths and classified 11,001 homes as high risk among the 60,785 assessed . In El Junquito, Caracas, 28-year-old Valeria gave birth to her son Edrick in the street on 24 June, after being evacuated from the maternity ward where she was in labour. Three months later, she, her husband and their 2 children are still sleeping in a tent beside their building while the area is assessed. Families face daily fear “Every day we face worry, fear, and dread. The rains are another issue, on top of the damage to the building where we live. When there are aftershocks, those are the moments when we go on alert. It never stops. Every day is one thing after another,” said Valeria. As Valeria described, rain is much more than just an inconvenience for families who have been living in tents beside damaged buildings for 3 months. The rain seeps in through cracks in the structures, heightening fears that they could collapse. The National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology has confirmed the development of a ‘super El Niño’ that is expected to intensify between September and December. Despite this, overall rainfall is predicted to decrease as dozens of tropical waves move through the country, bringing the kind of sudden, localised downpours that Valeria describes. Education interrupted The nights are not the only thing that remains unsettled for families across the affected areas. According to the Ministry of Education, more than 900 educational institutions were damaged, including 11 that collapsed completely and 89 that sustained severe structural damage. Sixty-seven of these schools were functioning as transitional camps for displaced families, but the authorities have been working to clear them so that classes can resume safely. In La Guaira, the residential complex where 12-year-old Greymar lived was among the buildings damaged by the earthquakes, after one of its towers partially collapsed. As a result, her own building was left structurally unsafe. Three months on, she and her family have been moving between temporary accommodation as they wait to find out where they will live next. Greymar has returned to school without seeing any familiar faces, including her friends. “Many of my friends died. And I won’t see my teacher anymore, because my teacher left La Guaira,” said Greymar. For children in these communities, returning to school does not mean that daily life has returned to normal. Many attend school during the day, but at home, many issues remain unresolved three months on. Support for children and families Plan International and its partners are running temporary learning and child-friendly spaces in areas where schools have been damaged. Where fear and disruption persist at night, the organisation provides psychosocial support to help children and their caregivers process their experiences. “One of the main challenges we’re facing right now is providing enough capacity and resources to reach everyone currently in transitional camps, as well as for the next stages of this response, like the safe return to schools. Venezuela needs everyone’s support – education saves lives,” said Ignacio Lombo, Education in Emergencies Specialist at Plan. In the coming months, Plan and its partners will keep supporting families’ recovery, return children to safe learning, and provide access to health and protection services. So far, support has been provided to families through more than 8,200 service contacts. This figure reflects service entries rather than a confirmed count of unique individuals, as some people may have received more than one type of support. “Three months on, the emergency has not ended: it has transformed. Families like Valeria’s and children like Greymar are still living through it every day, between unsettled nights and a return to school that hasn’t brought back everything they lost. Alongside our partners, we remain with families at every step, with particular attention to women, girls and adolescents,” said Pietro de Nicolai, Plan’s Head of Mission in Venezuela. pk.title: World: Save the Children and Vodafone Foundation launch global partnership to support children before, during and after crises
pk.description: Country: World Source: Save the Children NEW YORK, 24 September 2026 - Save the Children and Vodafone Foundation have announced a new global humanitarian partnership at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, bringing together their humanitarian expertise, technology and global reach to better support children and communities before, during and after emergencies. The partnership will strengthen emergency preparedness and humanitarian response and expand access to Vodafone Foundation’s technology and connectivity solutions in some of the world's most challenging environments. The collaboration was announced as recent climate-linked emergencies around the world - including flash floods in Nepal, heatwaves and forest fires globally - as well as ongoing conflict and displacement, continue to put millions of children at risk. These crises underscore the importance of greater investment in resilient infrastructure, technology and partnerships that can help communities better anticipate, withstand and recover from emergencies. A key element of the partnership is Vodafone Foundation's donation of six Instant Network kits — portable communications systems that can rapidly restore connectivity when conventional networks are disrupted by disasters or conflict. Pre-positioned at humanitarian hubs around the world and deployed by Save the Children during emergencies, the kits will help response teams coordinate operations, assess needs and deliver life-saving assistance more quickly. Vodafone Foundation will provide the technology, training and technical support for the kits, while Save the Children will oversee secure routine testing and deployment. Instant Network has already been used by Save the Children during emergency responses, including in Mozambique, where the technology helped improve operational coordination. To mark the launch, Save the Children and Vodafone Foundation co-hosted a high-level roundtable at UNGA, bringing together leaders from government, humanitarian organisations, philanthropy and business to discuss what’s needed to prepare for increasingly frequent and complex humanitarian emergencies over the next decade. Inger Ashing, CEO, Save the Children, said: “Children must be at the heart of every humanitarian response and as recent crises in our world have shown us, we can no longer just react. Communities must be equipped with the tools to better anticipate, withstand and recover from emergencies and technology and better connectivity absolutely plays a vital role. That’s why Save the Children’s partnership with Vodafone Foundation is an important one that helps to better support communities in times of crisis.” Joakim Reiter, Vodafone Foundation Trustee and Chief External and Corporate Affairs Officer, Vodafone Group, said: “In a crisis, reliable connectivity can make a vital difference - helping responders coordinate more quickly, communities access the support they need and strengthening preparedness for the future. That’s why we’re pleased to partner with Save the Children, bringing together its humanitarian expertise with Vodafone Foundation’s technology and connectivity to support children and communities before, during and after emergencies.” The partnership builds on a longstanding relationship between Save the Children and Vodafone Foundation, including collaboration on Skills Upload Junior, part of Vodafone Foundation's wider work supporting young people's digital wellbeing, skills and resilience. The new global partnership extends this relationship into humanitarian preparedness and response. The partnership will also explore how Vodafone Foundation's TerraGuard software and Vodacom’s M-Pesa cash-transfer payments could strengthen humanitarian response. Integrating these technologies into Save the Children's systems could help teams anticipate risks and enable assistance to reach families faster and more efficiently. Vodafone Foundation will also support Save the Children’s Emergency Fund, enabling rapid response when crises occur and investment in action before disaster strikes. Vodafone Foundation will also join Save the Children’s Humanitarian Network, a community of partners committed to faster, more effective humanitarian action for children. Notes to editors About the partnership Save the Children and Vodafone Foundation have launched a new global humanitarian partnership to strengthen emergency preparedness and response. Vodafone Foundation is donating six Instant Network Kits to restore connectivity when conventional networks are disrupted, and the partners will explore how TerraGuard and Vodacom’s M-Pesa payments could help teams anticipate risks and deliver assistance more quickly. The partnership also includes support for Save the Children’s Children’s Emergency Fund and aims to raise £1 million through Vodafone employee fundraising. About Save the Children’s Children’s Emergency Fund In 2025 Save the Children raised £18 million for emergency responses while responding to crises across Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan, Myanmar and beyond delivering what children need most during an emergency – food, water, medical care and safe spaces. About Vodafone Foundation Vodafone Foundation uses Vodafone’s technology, people and philanthropy to support those impacted by health or humanitarian crises, abuse and the digital divide. Driven by a purpose to connect for good, Vodafone Foundation works with partners across its global footprint to deliver programmes that create safety, inclusion and opportunity for everyone. www.vodafonefoundation.org

pk.title: World: Charting Africa’s path to climate resilience: Why the continent must confront its data deficits
pk.description: Country: World Source: African Risk Capacity Opinion piece editorial by Jean Chrysostome Ngabitsinze UN ASG and Group Director General, African Risk Capacity (ARC) In an era where climate change is no longer a distant threat but an active disruptor of lives, livelihoods, and macroeconomic stability, Africa’s response mechanisms must be equal to the task. The escalating severity of climate events demands a fundamental shift in how we prepare and respond. As the continent transitions to proactive, predictable resilience, our tools must be of the highest calibre. Any effective disaster response mechanism must be anchored in high-quality, reliable data. Data is not merely an administrative asset; it is the foundational currency of modern climate resilience. To position Africa on a sustainable growth trajectory envisioned in the African Union’s Agenda 2063 - "The Africa We Want", we must also urgently build and sustain a robust, sophisticated African disaster data ecosystem to serve as the foundation of all climate action. Without ground-level data to feed into satellite models, instruments such as parametric insurance are left vulnerable to high basis risk. According to the World Meteorological Organization’s, the entire African continent, which is home to more than 1.5 billion people, only has one-eighth of the weather stations it needs. It also has one of the least developed weather and climate observation networks globally, therefore challenging data collection. During COP29 climate talks, U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for urgent action to overcome the shortage of data that plagues the continent and called for more investment in producing weather information. In his brief on Early Warning Systems for all, he remarked: “ Nearly half of humanity is in the danger zone... and the people of Africa are on the front lines. Yet, we are flying blind in vast parts of the continent due to a lack of basic weather observation data." At the African Risk Capacity (ARC), we have pioneered the shift from reactive response to preparedness by advancing disaster risk management and financing (DRMF) and parametric insurance. We prioritise the development of risk profiles, early warning systems and contingency plans. Our mandate to support African countries plan, prepare and respond to extreme weather events and disease outbreaks relies on state-of-the-art tools. However, as we scale these innovations, we must confront a fundamental truth: our response is only as good as the data that powers it. The power of data in disaster risk management and financing In the DRMF landscape, data is the engine. At ARC, data is central to everything we do, from designing complex disaster risk models and defining parametric insurance triggers to implementing rapid payouts and targeting vulnerable populations. Each stage of our unique value proposition - which integrates four critical elements of preparedness: capacity building, early warning, risk pooling, and risk transfer - is heavily dependent on the quality of data at our disposal. During capacity building, we equip stakeholders to effectively interpret and utilize this data to leverage ARC tool. In contingency planning, robust data guarantees that emergency decisions are well-informed. Similarly, risk profiling uses historical events to accurately guide preparedness, while during risk transfer, data enables governments to determine the precise amount of risk to shift to international markets. The benefits of high-quality, localised data are profound. Beyond enabling accurate hazard forecasting and precise impact estimation, such data allows us to design models that faithfully reconstruct past disaster events, building trust along the full value chain. Ultimately, it is the cornerstone of effective risk layering, enabling countries to strategically combine various financial instruments tailored to their unique risk profiles. At national level, accurate data also ensures that domestic policymakers can make highly informed, evidence-based decisions. The use of high-quality impact-based early warning systems remains critical in supporting response, but these must be powered by data to ensure their accuracy and effectiveness. In addition to prompting timely response to a threat, early warning systems also trigger pre-agreed contingency plans, enabling disaster management authorities to coordinate an appropriate response. Confronting our data deficits Despite its obvious value, a significant "data deficit" persists across many African countries. Primarily driven by fragmented and siloed systems; valuable climate, agricultural, and socio-economic data is often scattered across various stakeholders without an interoperable architecture to link them. This is further compounded by inconsistent data quality and historical gaps. Outdated and insufficient meteorological and hydrological networks, coupled with missing loss-and-damage records, make it exceedingly difficult to customize risk models to local realities. This deficit also creates a critical "last-mile" bottleneck. Even when sophisticated risk models perform flawlessly and payouts are successfully triggered, outdated or incomplete beneficiary lists and social protection registries can stall shock-responsive social assistance. Ultimately, when models cannot be calibrated with reliable, localized data, "basis risk", the discrepancy between model-estimated losses and actual losses on the ground-increases, thereby slowing down the very financial mechanisms designed to offer rapid, life-saving relief. Breaking silos: ARC’s collaborative solutions in action We are not waiting for perfect conditions to emerge; ARC is actively working with member states to build them. Our approach is to break down institutional silos and co-create solutions with local experts. Through our multi-disciplinary national Technical Working Groups (TWGs), we bring together experts from diverse government ministries and partner organizations to serve as an important collaborative mechanism. The TWG uses existing data to plan, prepare and respond to climate-induced and disease threats through targeted interventions, identifying critical gaps in the process. These collaborative efforts are already yielding tangible results. For instance, our strategic partnerships with African universities to develop highly accurate "crop masks" ensure that agricultural risk models reflect actual, localised farming patterns. We are also working closely with member states to systematically dismantle data bottlenecks. In Madagascar, we facilitated targeted data-collection initiatives to precisely define parameters for drought risk modelling. Meanwhile, in Zambia and Zimbabwe, ARC has supported the digitisation of social protection registries, given the important role that shock-responsive social protection plays in facilitating the timely delivery of ARC payouts during crises. By integrating disaster and vulnerability data collection into existing, periodic national data efforts, we are helping countries build sustainable, long-term data habits rather than relying on ad-hoc, project-based assessments. A call to action: Building Africa’s sovereign data ecosystem For effective climate response, we must treat disaster data as critical public infrastructure and invest in world-class tools that enable climate-smart development. To achieve this, ARC has initiated the establishment of a continental data centre, designed to strengthen technical capacity at all levels, improve the quality and availability of disaster risk data, promote seamless cross-border data sharing, and support the development of localized risk models that underpin sovereign disaster risk financing decisions. This initiative cannot be achieved in isolation. I call upon African governments, international donors, development partners, and scientific organisations to join ARC in this strategic endeavour. In addition to financial support, we need active partners to help us build this resilient, sovereign African data ecosystem. By investing in robust data systems today, we reduce basis risk, build confidence in early warning systems, ensuring that every Dollar spent on disaster response is guided by undeniable evidence. To realise " the Africa we want ," we must equip the continent with the sophisticated, data-driven tools. This is more than just managing risk; it is about safeguarding our communities, protecting development gains, and securing the prosperous, climate-resilient future envisioned in Agenda 2063. ^ https://climateinafrica.com/from-data-deficit-to-action-inside-the-launch-of-climate-in-africa/ ^ https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2024/africa-has-worlds-least-developed-weather-observation-network

pk.title: 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Report examines the drivers and constraints shaping global carbon neutrality at Tsinghua University forum
pk.description: BEIJING , Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global experts and policymakers gathered at Tsinghua University on September 22 for a high-level seminar on global carbon neutrality to launch the 2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Annual Progress Report, which examines the factors accelerating or constraining the transition across 198 countries and regions. The event was part of a series marking the fifth anniversary of the Institute for Carbon Neutrality (ICON) at Tsinghua University and the sixth anniversary of China's "dual carbon" goals. It also coincided with the beginning of China's 15 th Five-Year Plan period. The seminar brought together perspectives from government, academia and international organizations on the global transition. Speakers included Li Gao, Vice Minister of China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment; Zhang Laibin, Chair of the Academic Committee of China University of Petroleum (Beijing); Zeng Rong, Executive Vice President of Tsinghua University; and Erik Solheim, former UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UNEP, who delivered remarks via video. The seminar was chaired by He Kebin, Member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and Dean of the Tsinghua University Institute for Carbon Neutrality. Wang Can, professor at Tsinghua University presented the 2026 report, which draws on more than 200 indicators to assess progress toward carbon neutrality across 198 countries and regions, tracking progress and identifying the underlying drivers and constraints of the global transition. The report identifies several trends: A new phase of the low-carbon transition is emerging , increasingly driven by technological progress but shaped by broader system conditions. Mature technologies are accelerating , with wind and solar power, energy storage, and electric vehicles continuing to expand rapidly. System-level bottlenecks remain significant , including limited grid integration capacity, high financing costs, gaps in market mechanisms, and barriers to international technology diffusion. Emerging technologies face additional commercialization challenges . Clean hydrogen and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) continue to encounter constraints related to demand, infrastructure, and viable business models. Developing economies face particularly strong barriers , including high financing costs, trade barriers, and insufficient system capacity to absorb and deploy green technologies. The findings suggest that while technological costs are declining and deployment is accelerating, the pace and scale of the global transition increasingly depend on whether financing, infrastructure, markets, and international cooperation can develop alongside technological progress. The full report is available through Tsinghua University's Global Carbon Neutrality Progress Tracker at www.cntracker.tsinghua.edu.cn .

pk.title: Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak Democratic Republic of the Congo | Uganda Weekly External Situation Report 19, Data as of 20 September 2026
pk.description: Countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda Source: World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. Event description The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with Dungu Health Zone in Haut-Uélé Province, bordering South Sudan, being the latest affected, bringing the total number of health zones affected to 63 since the start of the outbreak. This latest geographic expansion heightens concern about further spread towards international borders, while transmission within the country remains increasingly heterogeneous across affected provinces and health zones. Since External Situation Report #18, a further 475 confirmed cases and 222 confirmed deaths have been reported, bringing the cumulative total to 7733 confirmed cases, including 3732 deaths [crude case fatality ratio (CFR 48.3%)], as of 20 September 2026. Ituri remains the principal focus, although its relative contribution continues to decline, accounting for 76.9% of cumulative confirmed cases, while substantial transmission continues in Nord-Kivu and persists in Haut-Uélé. At the national level, daily incidence remains high and fluctuating, with the seven-day moving average rebounding in early September before declining in the most recent days. This national pattern masks divergent provincial trajectories. Ituri continues a gradual decline from its late-July peak but remains at a high level, while Nord-Kivu experienced a marked increase, reaching its highest incidence in mid-September, followed by an apparent decline in recent days. Transmission in Haut-Uélé remains sustained but below its August peak, while Tshopo shows renewed activity from a low baseline. Bas-Uélé continues to report sporadic transmission, with no recent transmission evident in Sud-Kivu. Overall, the epidemic remains geographically heterogeneous, with recent declines in the principal transmission areas occurring alongside persistent low-level transmission and continued geographic expansion to new areas.

ae.title: 'Super El Niño' explained and how it will affect the weather
ae.description: BRUSSELS: The El Niño weather pattern developing in the Pacific Ocean could be one of the strongest on record, with the potential to cause floods, droughts, extreme heat and crop losses across the world. The phenomenon, which the World Meteorological Organization expects to reach peak intensity by early 2027, could result in 451,000 excess deaths by February, the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab said on Wednesday. Here's what you need to know. What is El Nino? El Niño is the warm phase of the naturally occurring El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycle, a climate pattern that influences weather around the world. It tends to cause higher global temperatures and disrupt rainfall pattens across large regions - meaning drought in some areas and heavy rains in others. El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years, when weakening trade winds result in warmer ⁠waters in the eastern Pacific. What makes an El Nino Super? Elevated Pacific Ocean temperatures are the telltale sign that El Niño is forming. This month equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures hit 3.05 degrees Celsius (5.49 Fahrenheit) above normal levels - the highest temperature anomaly for any El Niño since records began, and far above the 0.5°C threshold for defining the phenomenon, data from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or NOAA, showed. The government agency formally declared El Niño conditions had begun in June. Equatorial Pacific temperatures of 0.5°C above the norm constitute a weak El Niño, versus 1.0°C for a moderate one, 1.5°C for a strong one, and 2.0°C for a very strong one, according to NOAA. The WMO does not officially use the term super, but forecast this month that the developing El Niño will intensify into "a very strong event" with significant impacts on rainfall and temperatures. The last strong El Niño in 2023 to 2024, combined with climate change, pushed 2024 to become the planet's hottest year on record. That year, Bolivia and Venezuela suffered disastrous fires, torrential floods hit Nepal, Sudan and Spain, and heatwaves in Mexico and Saudi Arabia killed thousands. Is El Nino linked to climate change? El Niño is a natural climate pattern and is not caused by climate change. However, global warming can make El Niños more intense. Greenhouse gas emissions have increased the ⁠planet's average temperature by around 1.4C since pre-industrial times. That higher baseline supercharges the effects of El Niño - enabling higher temperature spikes, more intense droughts, rains and the resulting disasters, including bushfires, floods and crop failures. Some scientists have said the destruction likely from this year's El Niño could provide a foretaste of extremes that will become the ⁠norm in the coming decades even ⁠without an El Niño, as a result of human-caused global warming. What to expect from this El Nino? The combination of climate change and El Niño has led the WMO to warn that 2027 could be the hottest year since records began. Of the 451,000 excess heat-related deaths that the ⁠coming El Niño could cause, Nigeria is expected to suffer 31,400, followed by Indonesia with 19,300 and Sudan with 17,600, the Climate Impact Lab said. Emergency response efforts, including early warning systems and protection for outdoor workers, could save tens of thousands of these lives, the researchers said. Typically, regions such as southern South America and parts of Central Asia get more rain in an El Niño, which can trigger disastrous flooding. In 2024, floods in Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil killed more than 180 people and displaced 600,000. Southern Africa, Central America and Australia tend to dry out, with potentially severe consequences for crop yields and energy production from hydropower. Rice exporters expect the harvest in India, the world's top producer, to decline this year by the most since 2009 to 2010, when an El Niño-induced drought curtailed production. Nearly 50 million people are at risk of acute hunger by the end of 2027 as a result of the developing El Nino, with southern Africa and South America among the worst-hit regions, according to U.N. World Food Programme forecasts. El Niño also intensifies heatwaves, including in regions far from the Pacific, such as Europe, and tends to increase hurricane activity in the central and eastern Pacific ocean.
